.husky/commit-msg.IMPLICIT: scans this commit's finished message for a GitHub closing keyword before an issue reference and refuses the commit on a hit (docs/agents/rules/commit-closes-keyword.txt), and a subject over 72 characters (scripts/lib/commit-subject.js), on every route but a replay. Then, but on a merge, refuses a commit whose staged diff weakens a check its message names on no `Weakens:` line (scripts/check-weakens-line.js). All three run in one Node process, scripts/commit-msg-dispatch.js (lib/commit-msg-rows.js, #5207), whose absence refuses every commit. Last, on every route a replay included, sources the adopter's own `.husky/commit-msg.local` where it exists, after refusing every commit on a script it names that the repo lacks (scripts/lib/local-hook.sh) or where mktemp cannot make the file that hands it `$route`.
.husky/commit-msg.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — the keyword closes the issue server-side on the push, so the guard-issue-close core never fires and the issue closes with no resolution comment and no `**Outstanding:**` line (#118); a subject over 72 characters breaks `git log --oneline` (#2172); and a check weakened inside a large commit goes unseen until it bites (#2203).
.husky/commit-msg.DEFEAT: `--no-verify`, which DOES skip this hook (unlike `prepare-commit-msg`), plus `HUSKY=0` and `core.hooksPath` pointed off `.husky/_`. `scripts/guard-dispatch.js` (its `guard-commit-form` core) denies `--no-verify` in an agent session unless wrapped; `scripts/lib/commit-form.js`'s LIMITS holds the whole defeat list (#800).

.husky/post-checkout.IMPLICIT: where node_modules links a dependency store the checked-out lockfile no longer keys, re-points it at the store standing for that lockfile, or names the attach command where none stands.
.husky/post-checkout.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a worktree left on the old store runs every test and tsc against a tree built for another lockfile; git ignores post-checkout's exit status once the checkout is done.
.husky/post-checkout.DEFEAT: no flag; skipped when scripts/lib/relink-store.sh, scripts/session-checkout.js or node is missing.

.husky/post-commit.IMPLICIT: prints the unpushed count after a commit that leaves any unpushed, what it released and what it kept after a session's commit, a fault notice after a commit that added one or whose comparison could not be read, a one-line note after a merge or a repo's first commit, a census notice after a commit that changed a guard the instruction-surface census measured, a registry notice after a commit that changed a guard whose guard-registry prose was anchored, a notice after an amend that dropped the amended commit's Review-Tier: line, after a commit that changed package-lock.json, where node_modules links a dependency store the merged lockfile no longer keys re-points it at the store standing for that lockfile or names the attach command where none stands, drops this session's whole-file claim on every path the commit touched where all the session's own hunks have landed, records it in the session's commit ledger, and — where a shim exists or a script was deleted since the keeper's last run — writes an exit-0 shim at each hook script a live session's hook lines still name but the main checkout no longer has, and deletes each shim no live session needs.
.husky/post-commit.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — unpushed work and a self-inflicted red are otherwise invisible, and git ignores this hook's exit status; the release drops only a claim of this session's own, only where none of its own hunks is left uncommitted, and a dropped claim is retaken by this session's next write to the file; the record writes only the session's own commit, into its own records; an expired census row or registry anchor is otherwise named only by the daily run, to nobody holding the change; a session started before a port runs its old hook line until it ends, and a deleted script on a fail-closed line refuses every call that line matches; a worktree left on the old store runs every test and tsc against a tree built for another lockfile.
.husky/post-commit.DEFEAT: no flag or env var for the five reporters; every block but the unpushed count, the shim keeper and the amend notice is skipped mid-replay (lib/commit-route.js's post-commit-stand-down set) or where the route will not read, and the release and the record by unsetting CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; blocks 1-8 are all skipped, with one line saying so, when scripts/post-commit-dispatch.js is missing or will not load; the relink takes no flag and is skipped when scripts/lib/relink-store.sh or scripts/session-checkout.js is missing.

.husky/post-merge.IMPLICIT: where node_modules links a dependency store its merged lockfile no longer keys, re-points it at the store standing for that lockfile, or names the attach command where none stands; and where a shim exists or a script was deleted since the keeper's last run, writes an exit-0 shim at each hook script a live session's hook lines still name but the main checkout no longer has, and deletes each shim no live session needs.
.husky/post-merge.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a worktree left on the old store runs every test and tsc against a tree built for another lockfile; a session started before a port runs its old hook line until it ends, and a deleted script on a fail-closed line refuses every call that line matches; git ignores post-merge's exit status.
.husky/post-merge.DEFEAT: no flag; the relink skipped when scripts/lib/relink-store.sh, scripts/session-checkout.js or node is missing, the keeper when scripts/keep-hook-shims.js or node is.

.husky/pre-applypatch.IMPLICIT: runs gitleaks over the applied patch's staged content, on every `git am` and every `git rebase --apply` replay, and refuses the apply on anything but a pass. Only a refusal starts node: scripts/pre-applypatch-refusal.js names the route and its abort; where it is missing, node is missing or it fails, the hook still refuses, printing one line that the route could not be named.
.husky/pre-applypatch.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a patch applied from a file is bytes no commit in this repository ever carried, which is the shape a pasted credential arrives in, and AGENTS.md §Secrets boundary makes a committed key permanent. A gate skipped here runs next only in CI, after the push, by which time the key is published.
.husky/pre-applypatch.DEFEAT: `git am --no-verify`, which abbreviates down to `--no-v`, skips this hook; `git rebase --apply` accepts no such flag. `scripts/guard-dispatch.js` (its `guard-commit-form` core) denies the flag only unwrapped, so an agent can still reach it; that core's LIMITS (`scripts/lib/commit-form.js`) holds every route past this hook (#800). WFC_GITLEAKS names the scanner's binary (§N7, #224), which on this hook is the whole gate.

.husky/pre-commit.IMPLICIT: runs every gate below on each commit — the shared-tree branch check, the linters, the secret scan and the repo checkers — and refuses the commit on a red. Deliberately not enumerated: this file has carried ~14 gates and gains more, and a list here is one that goes stale (mantahostels#1261).
.husky/pre-commit.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a commit is the last local moment before work is shared, and a gate skipped here runs next only in CI, after the push: the lander's run on that push (#2413).
.husky/pre-commit.DEFEAT: WFC_ALLOW_BRANCH=1 skips the shared-tree branch check alone, and WFC_ALLOW_GATE_INPUT_DELETE=1 lets one commit delete a staged gate's own required input, for the rare deliberate retirement (mantahostels#2894; the limb is in scripts/lib/precommit-gate.sh, so it reaches every staged_gate caller at once). Both are the founder's to set, and the guard-hook-escape core refuses an agent's spelling of either (#916). WFC_GITLEAKS names the secret scanner's binary (§N7, #224), so a value that exits 0 on everything defeats the scan alone. Its one argument, `--gates=merge` or `--gates=batch`, narrows a run the queue lander makes itself (#4545); git passes none, so no commit reaches it. The stack itself has no escape flag: --no-verify does not skip it, since .husky/prepare-commit-msg runs it and is the one hook that can refuse a commit and that the flag leaves running (mantahostels#1705), and the guard-commit-form core denies that flag on `git commit` and `git merge` both. Defeats remain: HUSKY=0 among those disarming every hook (the whole list: scripts/lib/commit-form.js's LIMITS), and a caller setting WFC_TEST_STAMP or WFC_MUTATION_STAMP by hand to a stamp it wrote itself in the git directory, which stands the declared test gate or the mutation hold down (scripts/lib/commit-key.js, scripts/mutation-hold-gate.js; #1650, #1910).

.husky/pre-merge-commit.IMPLICIT: runs the whole of .husky/pre-commit over the merge's own content.
.husky/pre-merge-commit.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a merge is the only route onto main that ran no gate at all, and a committed key is permanent (AGENTS.md §Secrets boundary). The whole stack rather than gitleaks alone, because a merge RESULT can break a cross-file check that both parents pass on their own: the doc map's coverage, the roadmap/digest version pair, the guard registry. `git diff --cached` here is the merge delta against `ours`, not the tree, so every `--staged`/`--cached` read in pre-commit is already scoped to it.
.husky/pre-merge-commit.DEFEAT: `git merge --no-verify` skips this hook and `commit-msg` both — but not the gates: `.husky/prepare-commit-msg` runs them, that being the one hook that can refuse a commit and that the flag leaves running, and `scripts/guard-dispatch.js` (its `guard-commit-form` core) denies the spelling in an agent session too (mantahostels#1705). What is left is `HUSKY=0` and `core.hooksPath` pointed off `.husky/_`, which turn off every hook at once — the whole list is that core's LIMITS (`scripts/lib/commit-form.js`, #800).

.husky/pre-push.IMPLICIT: where the range touches a mod folder in scripts/run-mod-tests.js's MODS, runs that mod's plugin tests at the pushed sha and refuses the push on a failure; reads the lander's green ledger and refuses a push to `main` of a sha it does not hold, and runs the guard-registry check over a queue ref's pushed sha against `origin/main`'s tip, and refuses a push that adds a fault, and appends each queue ref it pushes, with its sha and the time, to the queue log (scripts/lib/queue-log.js); where the code repo is apart from the tracker, reads every ref of a remote naming the tracker and refuses a push to the code repo of a sha sharing history with one.
.husky/pre-push.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — the mods' tests otherwise run only in the scheduled sweep (#1854), hours after the push, so this catches a broken mod before adopters can pull it; and the publish guard sees only Claude Code's Bash route, so this is the one local refusal of an untested `main` from the founder's terminal or a script (#2261); and the pre-commit registry gate judges the committing tree, so a commit from a diverged branch or a re-anchor computed on another base expires a row on `main` unseen (#3074); and nothing on the public code repo can refuse a push carrying the tracker's history, which once pushed is published for good (#1954).
.husky/pre-push.DEFEAT: `git push --no-verify` skips all four, and nothing denies it. The mod check warns and passes where the `claude` binary is missing, unusable or its run cannot finish, and refuses only on an exit of 2 or more, so a crashed or unreachable checker never fails a push; the landing gate likewise refuses only on an exit of 2 or more, and passes, printed, where it cannot read the config, the ref list, the repo root or the pushing tree; the landing registry gate does the same, and passes, printed, a push in a clone holding no `origin/main` or whose git will not resolve it, and one whose check cannot answer; the public-repo gate passes, printed, where it cannot read the config, the ref list or the pushing tree, and past the destination check refuses on any fault, a clone with no remote naming the tracker included. In a bare repository, which has no tree, they run only from `WFC_PLUGIN_ROOT`, each failing to load and passing without it.

.husky/prepare-commit-msg.IMPLICIT: runs the whole of .husky/pre-commit over the staged (or merge) content, on every commit that reaches this hook — EXCEPT on the replay path below (cherry-pick, rebase, `rebase --continue`), where it runs gitleaks alone and, on a cherry-pick, the review hold (mantahostels#1706, #3905). It also refuses a message carrying a GitHub closing keyword before an issue reference, on every route but a replay and a message still to be typed into $EDITOR (#138). On a commit that passes, writes the review hold's `Review-Tier:` trailer through scripts/review-tier-trailer.js (#3664), which refuses a tree that moved after the hold passed and fails the hold on re-reading it (#3905). Every step is a row of scripts/lib/prepare-commit-msg-rows.js, run in one Node process by scripts/prepare-commit-msg-dispatch.js (#5207), which reads the route through scripts/lib/commit-route.js; a missing dispatcher refuses every commit. Every step but the inline pre-commit runs under scripts/lib/hook-bound.sh's wall-clock limit, and one that hangs refuses the commit (#5213).
.husky/prepare-commit-msg.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — this is the one hook that can refuse a commit and that `--no-verify` leaves running, and a gate skipped here runs next only in CI, after the push.
.husky/prepare-commit-msg.DEFEAT: `HUSKY=0`, and `core.hooksPath` pointed off `.husky/_`, which turn off every hook in the repo at once; WFC_HOOK_LIMIT_S moves the limit. `scripts/guard-dispatch.js` (its `guard-commit-form` core) denies `--no-verify` on `git commit`, `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git cherry-pick` and `git revert` in an agent session unless wrapped; `scripts/lib/commit-form.js`'s LIMITS holds the whole defeat list (#800). Which binary the replay path's scan runs is named by WFC_GITLEAKS (§N7, #224).

scripts/audit-escape-lines.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, at most once in six hours, starts a detached batch — as no session's process, in a systemd user scope of its own stopped after 45 minutes where a user manager answers (#4706) — that reads every seat's transcripts for this repo and sends each close question block that passed on an escape line, and each re-send of a refused question as its whole message, with its refused block and the tool calls and session text between, gitleaks-swept, to the Vercel AI Gateway.
scripts/audit-escape-lines.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — it refuses nothing, a missing key, SDK or gitleaks sends nothing, and a store that will not read reports that rather than zeros; #671 made the loosening reversible on this evidence.
scripts/audit-escape-lines.js.DEFEAT: `WFC_ESCAPE_AUDIT=0` for a session stops the batch starting.
scripts/audit-escape-lines.js.TREE: host — judges escape lines in transcripts filed under the host root's project slug

scripts/check-ci-status.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start (its hook passing --write, without which neither the dispatch nor the filer launch below happens, #4449), asks GitHub whether the last sweep on the branch went red, injects the verdict into the session's context, dispatches a sweep the session never asked for when that verdict has gone stale (mantahostels#1816), and launches the red-suite filer — as no session's process, in a systemd user scope of its own stopped after 45 minutes where a user manager answers (#4706) — which files or comments on the tracker, where the daily filer did not (#2480).
scripts/check-ci-status.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — nothing reports a red between the local gates and the next sweep, so every detector here is a poll and this is the only one that fires unasked; a verdict nothing refreshes is the fault mantahostels#1816 measured at a 15h35m blind window; and a broken daily filer left a red unticketed for three days (#2480).
scripts/check-ci-status.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; --notify is silent unless the run it reads is red or the newest sweep is older than SWEEP_STALE_MS. The dispatch is capped by AUTOFIRE_COOLDOWN_MS and withheld where HEAD is already covered; the filer launch at one an hour, on the core host only.
scripts/check-ci-status.js.TREE: host — reports CI on `main` against the main checkout's own HEAD

scripts/check-harness-canary.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, reads the installed Claude Code version; where no probe has passed on it, launches, as no session's process in a systemd user scope of its own stopped after 45 minutes where a user manager answers (#4706), one detached `claude -p` haiku turn against a throwaway plugin, and prints a red verdict at each start until a version passes, or a fault reading its state file at the start that finds it (#3436).
scripts/check-harness-canary.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — nothing else notices a harness update restoring the listing cost or breaking every description-less skill, and an unreadable version or a failed probe is silence at start, never a block.
scripts/check-harness-canary.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; a later version that passes ends it, and `--probe` re-runs the probe by hand for a red suspected false.
scripts/check-harness-canary.js.TREE: host — probes the harness from a scratch directory

scripts/check-idle-efforts.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, reads every adopting checkout's tracker and reports a stopped refill loop, a live loop's damaged file and each tracker holding an effort idle past 2 days, or unread, whose finding was not yet shown that machine-local day; a dispatcher's or the loop's job start, or any job's resume, stamps none of it, and through the hooks shows none of it.
scripts/check-idle-efforts.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a stopped loop, or a route it skips, strands an effort with nothing else to say so.
scripts/check-idle-efforts.js.DEFEAT: none needed — it never blocks; deleting its delivery stamp names today's findings again.
scripts/check-idle-efforts.js.TREE: host — reads every served main checkout's launch stores

scripts/check-interop-latency.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, times one Windows policy query through the interop bridge, and a second where the first is slow; where both are slow, appends one evidence record to `.interop-degraded.jsonl` under .claude/tmp/markers and prints that the bridge is degraded with the sync-then-shutdown recovery; prints nothing on a fast or unprobeable bridge.
scripts/check-interop-latency.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a degraded bridge otherwise reads as load, and the record is the only trace of its cause once the VM restarts.
scripts/check-interop-latency.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; a `wsl --shutdown` clears the fault.
scripts/check-interop-latency.js.TREE: host — times the machine, logging under the host root's markers

scripts/check-kernel-stall.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, reads this boot's kernel log and the scheduler clock over 1 s and, where the log holds an RCU stall or the clock is frozen, prints that the VM is unhealthy and the sync-then-shutdown recovery, reading the Windows event log once where a stall's `t` is large; prints nothing on a clean or unreadable reading.
scripts/check-kernel-stall.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — nothing else tells a session the VM is unhealthy, and a reading it cannot take is silence, never a warning.
scripts/check-kernel-stall.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; a reboot of the VM clears a stall, the signal being per-boot, and a freeze clears once the clock moves.
scripts/check-kernel-stall.js.TREE: host — reads kernel state only, its report persisted in the host root's notify store

scripts/check-main-checkout-cutover.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start (`--notify`), reads the main checkout's upstream; where it is not cut over, lists the live sessions (`claude agents --json`) and, where none stands in the main checkout, runs the cutover (lib/cutover-run.js) — landing the main checkout's local commits through a queue ref, removing `main`'s upstream and running a levelling pass, which first restores to `HEAD` each blocking main-checkout edit `origin/main` already holds byte for byte, where every blocking edit is one (#5808) — and prints its report; where one does, prints a FAIL naming each; prints nothing once cut over. Run without `--notify`, as `npm run status` does, it reports a main checkout not cut over and cuts nothing.
scripts/check-main-checkout-cutover.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — otherwise a repo whose main checkout was never cut over shares one unguarded tree with nothing moving it (#4688), and the cutover waits on the founder's hands (#5247 Q1 (A)).
scripts/check-main-checkout-cutover.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; the cutover clears it.
scripts/check-main-checkout-cutover.js.TREE: host — reads and cuts over the main checkout

scripts/check-orphan-wait-loops.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, injects a report naming each orphaned wait loop still running on this machine — every time, while it runs. It never kills one.
scripts/check-orphan-wait-loops.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — such a loop is invisible to every other checker here, and a run that cannot read /proc reports nothing rather than calling a process orphaned.
scripts/check-orphan-wait-loops.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; --minutes <n> moves the threshold on a hand run.
scripts/check-orphan-wait-loops.js.TREE: none — sweeps the machine's process table

scripts/check-orphaned-edits.js.IMPLICIT: at session start, at most once a clock hour across the repository's worktrees (its hook passes --write --hourly), files each uncommitted tracked file that no live session owns once as a takes:triage issue, a linked worktree's together as one, printing nothing: in a linked worktree, or in a main checkout not yet cut over, once nobody has touched it for 24 hours; in a cut-over main checkout, at any age, save an edit `origin/main` already holds byte for byte on a path it has changed since `HEAD`, which levelling clears (#5808). It never reverts or writes the file.
scripts/check-orphaned-edits.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — an orphan voids certificates for days unseen, and any ownership signal that cannot be read silences the report rather than calling a live session's edit orphaned.
scripts/check-orphaned-edits.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook beyond its hourly throttle; --hours <n> moves the threshold on a hand run, save in a cut-over main checkout, which has none.
scripts/check-orphaned-edits.js.TREE: host — walks the main checkout, as git's common dir names it from whichever tree launched the run (#4483), and every linked worktree (#4244)

scripts/check-plugin-gap.js.IMPLICIT: on every SessionStart, injects a version-gap line, the adopter-upgrade rule text, the consent accept/decline commands and the in-session walk command into the session's context when the pin, supply and install disagree, or with them agreeing a walk-owed line where an accepted walk has not landed, else a materialised-not-live line where only this process lags, a predicted #258 ref-conflict line (#318) alongside it where the supply gap is open, and a `stepsOwed` block (#248) whenever that field holds an undeclined entry, and a stale-hook-root block (#1168) or an unresolved-shim block (#1839) — the latter three independent of the gap.
scripts/check-plugin-gap.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — otherwise a stale plugin runs with nothing saying so (#238).
scripts/check-plugin-gap.js.DEFEAT: for the gap report only, a decline for this exact repo+tag (scripts/lib/adopter-consent.js, #245); the three independent blocks have none.
scripts/check-plugin-gap.js.TREE: host — compares the main checkout's pinned, supplied and installed plugin and its git-hook shims

scripts/check-refill-loop-stop.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start but a dispatcher's or the loop's job, prints the refill loop's last stop where it was a damaged control file, where newer than the stamp, then stamps it; prints its newest first overflow launch where newer than that launch's stamp, then stamps it; and names a damaged state file, a stopped loop's damaged control file or a running loop's overlong restart wait.
scripts/check-refill-loop-stop.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — the loop runs outside any session, so nothing else reports its stopping, its spending or its sticking in a restart wait.
scripts/check-refill-loop-stop.js.DEFEAT: none needed — it never blocks; deleting a stamp names its last event again.

scripts/check-release-lag.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, reads the newest release tag's source, `origin/main`, each adopter checkout's pin and its installed version, and where the source is more than LAG_WARN_DAYS behind `origin/main`, or unreadable, or an adopter's install is not at its pin, or an adopter's main checkout stands behind its last fetched `origin/main` (with what a levelling pass would do, and what blocks it), prints that with the pins, installs and blockers it concerns; prints nothing otherwise. It fetches nothing and moves no checkout.

scripts/check-release-lag.js.TREE: host — reads the main checkout's tags and `origin/main`, the adopters' main checkouts and the config dir's install registry

scripts/check-seat-utilisation.js.IMPLICIT: at every session start, reads each seat's usage cache and injects a blocked-work notice when every live seat is exhausted, a tier-drop notice when a model's weekly allowance is spent on every readable seat, a SEAT UNREAD panel when an unread seat holds either back, and the gate-2 trial's pending, failed, review or cannot-honour notice; records one reading a day either way.

scripts/check-seat-utilisation.js.DEFEAT: none at the hook; --notify is silent unless one of those notices holds or the ladder declaration falls back (#410).
scripts/check-seat-utilisation.js.TREE: host — reads seat usage and the capacity ladder the host root's config names

scripts/clear-rule-latch.sh.IMPLICIT: at every compaction, deletes this session's (and its subagents') rule-injection latch markers from .claude/tmp/markers, so each relocated rule is handed to the session once more after its context is cut.
scripts/clear-rule-latch.sh.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a latch outliving the text it latched leaves a session holding neither the rule nor any prospect of being given it, which is worse than never having injected it.

scripts/concision-backstop.sh.IMPLICIT: records the session's base sha at SessionStart, and at Stop blocks the turn ending once per unmet signal — demanding the concision pass over prose added, or code-review over code changed or a declared sensitive path written or narrowed from the declaration; in an /implement session either nag ends with rule:implement-closing-steps, the only place a session meets those steps (#2031).

scripts/guard-automode-refusal.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a session that ends on a refusal stalls the ticket, and the remedy is one sentence saying which way it went.
scripts/guard-automode-refusal.js.DEFEAT: once per refused call and at most MAX_BLOCKS times per session and per subagent; silent where the turn carries no refusal, and on every failure path.

scripts/guard-dispatch.js.IMPLICIT: on a backgrounded Bash call (guard-bg-job) injects rule:killed-background-job; on a Write, Edit or NotebookEdit of a test file (inject-test-rules) injects base §X8, §X9 and §X10; on a Write, Edit or NotebookEdit of a hot-path program or a hook registration (inject-hot-path-cost) injects base §G13; on a Write or Edit adding a mantahostels#N citation the inherited tracker never used (guard-citation-tracker), names each such number and injects rule:citation-tracker; on a `gh` or issue-tracker Bash call (guard-tracker-rules) injects the tracker rules that call engages; on a Skill call loading `code-review` (guard-review-rules) injects the six review rules and this session's review subagent type, Artefact paths and standards base, and (inject-review-tier) the review tier the change's sensitive paths owe; on a Skill call loading `diagnosing-bugs` (inject-founder-wording) injects the four recurrence checks and the host's tracker corpus — each rule once per session and agent, latched under .claude/tmp/markers; on a `Write` to `.claude/tmp/` (guard-scratch-overwrite) appends that path to the session's record in `.claude/tmp/markers/` (#1167); before a Bash command writing a tier-1 path a live neighbour holds (guard-claimed-bash-write), injects those claims within a 2,000 B session budget, credits an uncontended code target to the write ledger (mantahostels#2778), notes an inline program's quoted paths and a deletion's tracked files on the selection ledger (#1220, #1791), and hands over rule:whole-file-restore on a restore over uncommitted changes (#2028); scripts/guard-dispatch.js.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — none of these rules has an enforcing guard before the act, so the moment of the call is the only one at which each can still shape it (mantahostels#1904, #1887, #2015), and a vendored skill cannot carry project rules (mantahostels#2501, spec #1612, #628); the scratch record is convenience — it tells a session's own rewrite from a neighbour's clobber, without which every rewrite of an existing scratch file would be refused; a claim nobody has to remember to take is what makes a clobber by any route reportable and recoverable (mantahostels#295), and the Bash-route warning credits nothing a live neighbour holds; the supplied `Artefact:` line is convenience — the session would have added it after a refusal, at the cost of re-issuing the whole prompt (#482) — and the routing file is the founder's own ruling, burn mode his own switch (#4919, #5033); the hook-escape refusal is fail-safe — a commit past a stood-down gate lands on the shared `main`, and the escape is the founder's judgement (#916); the test-timeout refusal is fail-safe — it costs one re-sent call, where the run it stops holds the session blocked for its whole length (#5798); the chrome-merge refusal is fail-safe — a merged note breaks the one JSON line the caller parses, and the tab report in it is lost (#5381); the issue-link refusal is fail-safe — GitHub accepts a link that closes a loop of open issues, and the link commands are the only place it is checked (#5055); the phase-scope record is fail-safe — a guard allowing unchecked in silence would report itself as protecting work it never judged (mantahostels#147), and where no roadmap exists there is no card phase to judge, so its silence reports nothing false (#5576); the suite-concurrency notices are fail-safe — a session that cannot tell a neighbour's half-written file from its own breakage debugs the wrong thing, and the launch is the last moment before the verdict it will misread; the unasked-rerun refusal is fail-safe — it costs one re-typed command, and the run it stops is one the push and `result:` gates already do not need; the load-wait refusal is fail-safe — a wait gated on machine load ends only when other work stops, so its cost lands on other sessions and the founder, where a refusal costs one re-typed command (#5325); the vitest-wrapper and ugrep-pattern notes are fail-safe — a parked worker and a refused pattern are each silent, so the launch is the last moment to say so (mantahostels#2002, #1021 Q1); the npm-install refusal is fail-safe — a package's `preinstall` runs as the founder before anything reads it, and anyone can pre-register a hallucinated name (Spracklen et al., USENIX Security 2025); the pip-install refusal is fail-safe on the same grounds, an sdist's build code running as the founder at install; the browser-profile refusal is fail-safe — a tab opened in another account's profile hands the founder a page signed in as the wrong subscription (#5339); the practice-note list and refusal are fail-safe — a note named off the craft list is one no gate can later find (#2258, #5344). The PostToolUse cores are fail-safe: each sees what only the answered call shows — its response, the file as written, the bytes a shell changed — and none refuses (#2787).
scripts/guard-dispatch.js.DEFEAT: `scripts/clear-rule-latch.sh` clears the latch and a rule is said again; `sensitivePaths` declared, `[]` included, silences the review tier's undeclared line; a `citation-exempt: #N` on the line passes the citation core; the scratch-overwrite refusal is escaped by re-sending the same call, by design (#1728), and its record has none; a Bash write by a spelling the claimed-bash-write routes do not name passes unseen; `WFC_SUITE_DETACH=1` or `WFC_SUITE_TIMEOUT=1` as a prefix passes the suite-background core; `WFC_TEST_TIMEOUT=1` as a prefix, or a suite the snapshot does not cover in the same command, passes the test-timeout core; a suite launched from inside a script never reaches the suite-concurrency core (mantahostels#2024); a load wait in a script file the shell runs, a load read spelled through a variable or a command the load-wait core does not name, or reaching a `break` through a variable no `name=` or `read` assigned it to, a bare name in `[[…]]` or a nested `if`'s `fi`, and an interpreter's own polling loop with no shell loop around it pass the load-wait core; re-typing the command, any flag but `--queue`, a file filter, or `bash -c`, a script or a heredoc wrapping the launch passes the unasked-rerun core; a sweep fired from the web UI, `gh api … /dispatches`, a script or the founder's terminal never reaches the sweep-fire core; a merge made for the whole shell or a group, one inside a `-c` string and a launch from a script file pass the chrome-merge core; a link made in the web UI or by a script's child `gh` never reaches the issue-link core, `scripts/check-issue-cycles.js` its backstop; `session-arbiter.js release [--force] <path>` drops a claim the file-claim core took; naming a real path in the prompt leaves the `Artefact:` line alone, and `scripts/burn-mode.sh off` ends the burn remap; WFC_NO_ECHO_CHAIN=1 stops the echo record and WFC_NO_IMAGE_BUDGET=1 the image count; `WFC_ALLOW_NEW_PACKAGE=1` in the environment Claude Code was started in stands down the npm-install and pip-install cores' registry checks alone, and the same assignment on the command line is never honoured (mantahostels#109); a docs/called-cards.md row for a card the founder has called escapes the phase-scope deny, its fail-open record having none; listing a core's name (`guard-bg-job`, `inject-test-rules`, `inject-hot-path-cost`, `guard-citation-tracker`, `guard-scratch-git`, `guard-job-dir-scratch`, `guard-root-scratch`, `guard-scratch-overwrite`, `guard-self-match`, `guard-wait-loop`, `guard-suite-background`, `guard-test-timeout`, `guard-sweep-fire`, `guard-claimed-bash-write`, `guard-file-claim`, `guard-review-rules`, `inject-review-tier`, `inject-founder-wording`, `guard-tracker-rules`, `guard-branch-publish`, `guard-branch`, `guard-commit-form`, `guard-anthropic-report`, `guard-cpu-load`, `guard-check-sh`, `guard-issue-body`, `guard-issue-link`, `guard-issue-close`, `guard-issue-create-label`, `guard-issue-phase-scope`, `guard-headroom-read`, `guard-hook-escape`, `guard-chrome-merge`, `guard-suite-concurrency`, `guard-unasked-rerun`, `guard-vitest-wrapper`, `guard-root-find`, `guard-ugrep-pattern`, `guard-registry-atomicity`, `guard-pull-form`, `guard-push-rules`, `guard-node-heap`, `guard-rm-unchecked`, `guard-npm-install`, `guard-pip-install`, `guard-recursive-dot-read`, `guard-wide-read`, `guard-agent-poll`, `guard-echo-call`, `guard-dispatch-rewrite`, `guard-blind-dispatch`, `record-tool-echo`, `post-write`, `refresh-claims`, `scan-injection`, `guard-image-budget`, `guard-typecheck-red`, `guard-browser-profile`, `guard-practice-note`) under the host's `disabled` silences that core alone, and listing `guard-dispatch.js` silences every core.

scripts/session-start-sweeps.sh.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a session's descendant that outlives it otherwise runs on unseen, reparented to `/init` (#4332, #4335). Deliberate self-throttling leaves no limit record anywhere, so nothing else on this machine can see it — the readings are collected against the day a seat is cut, the transcripts behind them ageing off at ~30 days (mantahostels#1404). The container sweep is fail-safe both ways: `takes:children` routes to no command, so a container whose last child has closed is offered to nobody and sits on the frontier indefinitely (mantahostels#1632), and a `takes:to-tickets` left on an already-ticketed spec routes to a command that duplicates those tickets (mantahostels#1663) — every value it moves to is fixed by `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`, not chosen by the script. And the gc job is what keeps `.git` from growing without bound (mantahostels#1175): `git gc` (no `--aggressive`, no `--prune=now`) only deletes objects both unreachable AND past the 2-week `gc.pruneExpire` default, which is worktree-aware (a live worktree's HEAD counts as reachable) and is the arbiter's own stated assumption for when a superseded `priorBlobs` entry stops being recoverable (arbiter-store.js's `claimVersions`). And the close-check reading would otherwise reach the founder only when someone thought to ask for it, which spec #1091 rules out (#1104), and so would the round-check reading (#1711), and the flip-line reading (#2331). And the suite's queue wait decays as the suite grows, unseen until a backlog is bad enough for the founder to open another cut-map (#1147, #1157). And the architecture scan has no other trigger in any repo (#1348, #1320 Q2 (A)). And the heresy sweep has no other trigger in any repo (#3365). And a repo's own tracker, roadmap, manual and doc-map checks run nowhere else in an adopter, so drift there goes unseen (#1510, #1407 Q2 (A)). And a queue ref push the push hook never saw, or a lander that died mid-batch, would otherwise hold every landing back until the next push (#2405). And the lander runs outside any session, so nothing else reports it stalling or dying (#2406). And with every session closed nothing else sweeps, which is how a dead session's vitest workers spun for eight hours (#4342). And a Chrome child's tab group can be closed only by a resume of its own session, so a closer the launcher's trap missed — the launcher SIGKILLed, the machine asleep, Chrome closed — is retried nowhere else, and its tabs stay in the founder's Chrome (#5368, #5385).

scripts/vitest-pass-reporter.ts.IMPLICIT: records every suite run's verdict, scope and closure, the files the launcher's pass store cached folded in, for the globalSetup teardown to stamp into the pre-push marker, and each file's own verdict and imports for the pass store (#4790), writes that marker itself on an empty selection, and prints a line on a filtered or unrecorded scope.
scripts/vitest-pass-reporter.ts.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — that marker is the only thing keyed to a sha (mantahostels#910), and any doubt leaves no certificate.
scripts/vitest-pass-reporter.ts.DEFEAT: none — naming any reporter replaces the default set, so dropping it means editing vitest.config.ts.

scripts/vitest-temp-root.ts.IMPLICIT: on every suite run, makes `<os.tmpdir()>/wfc-vitest-<pid>-XXXXXX`, hands it to the workers, whose setup file points `TMPDIR` at it, and removes it at teardown, with every fixture a test left in it.
scripts/vitest-temp-root.ts.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a test that never removes its fixture otherwise leaves it in the machine's `/tmp` for good (#5081).
scripts/vitest-temp-root.ts.DEFEAT: none — the wrapper keeps the real temp root, so the suite queue and its hand-off files never move.

scripts/vitest-tree-watch.ts.IMPLICIT: on every suite run, names the tracked files rewritten while the suite ran, and, outside a rowless run (lib/pass-store.js: the lander's or ci.yml's), removes the read audit's log directories killed runs left (#5046) and arms the audit on NODE_OPTIONS for every worker and the Node children it spawns (#4916), under which a stub, a shell or a checkout program a test runs in the checkout, or hands a path there, runs traced by `strace`, where one works, tracer and child on one CPU (#4966, #4982, #5132), and each real git and the git guard is handed an event log of the audit's on `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` (#4997); and, on a verdict the reporter left, records the run's certificate (none where its scope hit the task cap) or red marker in the canonical checkout's marker store, and each file it ran in the pass store (#4790), none keyed on an input whose change time passed a mark the setup took as the run began (#5018), the certificate being what the pre-push gate reads; on a red one it names which failures were already red on the run's base (#3624).
scripts/vitest-tree-watch.ts.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — a red caused by a file saved mid-run is otherwise read as a breakage in the code under test (mantahostels#273).
scripts/vitest-tree-watch.ts.DEFEAT: none — it prints and records, and never fails a run.

scripts/write-self-plugin-marker.sh.IMPLICIT: writes a `.self-plugin-loaded-<session id>` marker holding CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT under `.claude/tmp/markers/` at every session start, unasked (#2438).
scripts/write-self-plugin-marker.sh.JUSTIFIED: fail-safe — the marker is the canary's only proof the self-plugin's guards loaded, and from where; without it every session is refused.
scripts/write-self-plugin-marker.sh.TREE: host — writes this session's self-plugin marker into the host root's markers
